title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 26
paragraphs: Then, in the arranging of the various posts, there arose much heated argument between the Tegeans and the Athenians, for each claimed to occupy the other wing of the army themselves, citing deeds both new and old. The Tegeans said: “We have always been judged worthy of this post by the whole body of allies in every joint expedition the Peloponnesians have made, whether long ago or recently, ever since the time when the sons of Heracles tried, after the death of Eurystheus, to return to the Peloponnese. We gained this honor then because of this event: when we, with the Achaians and the Ionians then in the Peloponnese, had come out to the Isthmus to help and were encamped opposite those wishing to return, Hyllos is said to have proposed that it was not right for one army to risk its safety in battle with the other, and urged instead that the man whom the Peloponnesian army judged to be the best of them should fight Hyllos himself in single combat on terms agreed between them. The Peloponnesians resolved that this should be done, and they swore an oath together on this condition: if Hyllos conquered the Peloponnesians' chosen man, then the sons of Heracles should return to their father's inheritance; but if he were conquered, then the sons of Heracles should depart and lead away their army and not try for a hundred years to return to the Peloponnese. Of all the allies there was chosen — he himself making a voluntary offer — Echemos son of Aëropos son of Phegeus, who was our commander and king. He fought a single combat and killed Hyllos. Because of this deed, we obtained among the Peloponnesians of that time — besides many other great privileges we still possess — this one too: always leading the other wing of the army whenever a joint expedition is made. To you Lacedaemonians we offer no opposition, and we give you the choice of whichever wing you wish to command; but of the other, we say, it belongs to us to lead, as in former times. And apart from this deed just related, we are worthier than the Athenians to hold this post, for we have fought many glorious contests against you, Spartans, and many against others too. So it is just that we have the other wing rather than the Athenians, since they have performed no such deeds as ours, old or new.”
